cohort: The study included 178 antenatal women between 11-13 weeks of gestation visiting the OPD of an institute of obstetrics and Gynecology.
finding: Combining three risk factors—previous history of pre-eclampsia, mean arterial pressure (MAP), and uterine artery pulsatality index (Ut. AtPI)—was more effective in predicting adverse pregnancy outcomes, with a sensitivity of 86.8% and specificity of 44.9% for preeclampsia.
